title: Next.js
label: Next.js
desc: React framework that renders on the server and bundles a router, data layer, and build pipeline for full-stack apps.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Scaffold an App Router project with the official CLI, then start the dev server on port 3000.

snippets.code:
# Create a TypeScript app with the recommended defaults
npx create-next-app@latest atlas --yes
cd atlas

# Start the dev server with Turbopack
npm run dev

sections.title: Project Structure
sections.description: Folders under app become URL segments, while reserved filenames decide what each segment renders.

snippets.code:
atlas/
  app/
    layout.tsx             root layout, always required
    page.tsx               route /
    (shop)/
      cart/page.tsx        route /cart, group name hidden
    guides/[slug]/page.tsx route /guides/:slug
    api/health/route.ts    GET /api/health
    _components/           private folder, never routable
  public/                  files served from /
  next.config.ts           build and runtime settings

sections.title: Routing
sections.description: A page file makes its folder public; bracketed segments capture URL values and arrive as a promise.

sections.title: Layouts
sections.description: A layout wraps every page beneath its folder, stays mounted across navigation, and the root one must render html and body.

sections.title: Server Components
sections.description: Components run on the server unless marked otherwise, so they can await data directly and keep secrets out of the bundle.

sections.title: Client Components
sections.description: The use client directive marks a module for the browser, enabling state, effects, and DOM event handlers.

sections.title: Data Fetching
sections.description: Await data inside server components; use cache gives the result a lifetime and cacheTag names it for invalidation.

sections.title: Route Handlers
sections.description: A route file exports one function per HTTP verb and receives a web Request plus the segment params.

sections.title: Metadata
sections.description: Export a metadata object or a generateMetadata function from a server page or layout to fill the head tags.

sections.title: Styling
sections.description: Global CSS, CSS Modules, and Tailwind are built in; module files keep class names local to one component.

sections.title: Images and Fonts
sections.description: next/image reserves layout space and optimizes formats, while next/font self-hosts typefaces during the build.

sections.title: Middleware
sections.description: Proxy, the file convention renamed from middleware in Next.js 16, runs before rendering to redirect, rewrite, or add headers.

sections.title: Deployment
sections.description: Build once with next build, serve with next start, or copy a standalone bundle into a small container image.

snippets.code:
# Produce the production bundle
npm run build

# Serve it; -p changes the port
npx next start -p 8080

FROM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:22-alpine AS run
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
COPY --from=build /app/public ./public
COPY --from=build /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=build /app/.next/static ./.next/static
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "server.js"]
